title: pvWriteIOSSWriter
body:
## pvWriteIOSSWriter

Explicit-export writer for Exodus II (.exo) through the IOSS library, the finite-element format of Sandia's SIERRA codes, Cubit and many structural and multiphysics solvers. It accepts a dataset, a partitioned dataset or a partitioned dataset collection; every partition becomes an element block unless selectors (or, for data read by ParaView's IOSS reader, its IOSS assembly) assign partitions to blocks and sets, and a time-dependent input is exported for the one scheduled time step: Schemaxis manages TimeStepRange and TimeStepStride, because the writer otherwise loops over every input time step itself. Publication uses the semantic contract: the file is re-read and geometry plus every input point and cell field are compared, accepting loss of structure, point identity, connectivity order and storage type. Use pvWriteExodusIIWriter for ParaView's older Exodus writer and pvWriteCGNSWriter for CGNS tools.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Exodus ids start at 1. For time-dependent input, ParaView 5.13.3's IOSS writer aborts the whole run when the point global ids start at 0 or are absent (native pvbatch probe, 2026-10-12), so Schemaxis refuses such an export before writing (UNSUPPORTED_INPUT): add ids with pvGlobalPointAndCellIds and set OffsetGlobalIds true, which the probe confirmed writes the scheduled step. Static input is written either way.
- vtkIOSSWriter runs its own time loop and ignores the scheduled time (vtkIOSSWriter.cxx:285-342). A native pvbatch 5.13.3 probe found that on creation ParaView replaces the static TimeStepRange [0, 1] with the domain range [0, n-1], and a default export wrote all steps for one scheduled time. When the exported node reports two or more time steps (read from its pipeline information, so filters count too), Schemaxis sets TimeStepRange [k, k+1] and TimeStepStride 2 for the scheduled step k (probe: exactly one step, whose Point Value matched step k, for k = 0, 2 and 9); both settings are managed and cannot be authored, and a scheduled time that is not one of the input steps gives TIME_NOT_IN_INPUT. The probe did not establish the time stamp stored in the file, so do not rely on it.
- ParaView's GUI-only entity-type chooser (EntityType, which has no native command) is not exposed; select blocks and arrays with the *Selectors and *Arrays settings.
- Semantic readback compares every input point and cell array by name. Exodus stores global ids as maps rather than fields, and readers may merge arrays whose names end in X, Y and Z into one vector, so inputs carrying such arrays (for example GlobalPointIds, or Point X/Y/Z) fail verification with 'semantic readback lacks an input field'; pass only the arrays you need with pvPassArrays before exporting.
- An earlier catalogue run (verification/2026-09-16-catalogue-expansion.json, writerQualification) passed only on a small serial fixture with default options; no current native acceptance check is recorded, so verify the export on representative data.

Native constructor: `IOSSWriter`. Identity: `writers/IOSSWriter`. Role: `writer`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Connect upstream object to `Input` | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":true,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection","vtkPartitionedDataSet","vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Assembly` | Select which assembly is used when specify selectors to choose blocks to write. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `ChooseArraysToWrite` | Property to control whether to choose arrays to write. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `DisplacementMagnitude` | If input dataset has displacements pre-applied, setting the displacement magnitude to non-zero ensures that the point coordinates in the dataset are correctly transformed using the displacement field array, if present. | `{"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `EdgeBlockArrays` | Select the edge block arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `EdgeBlockSelectors` | Specify the edge block selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `EdgeSetArrays` | Select the edge set arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `EdgeSetSelectors` | Specify the edge sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ElementBlockArrays` | Select the element block arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ElementBlockSelectors` | Specify the element block selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ElementSetArrays` | Select the element set arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ElementSetSelectors` | Specify the element sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FaceBlockArrays` | Select the face block arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FaceBlockSelectors` | Specify the face block selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FaceSetArrays` | Select the face set arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FaceSetSelectors` | Specify the face sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `NodeBlockArrays` | Select the node block arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `NodeSetArrays` | Select the node set arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `NodeSetSelectors` | Specify the node sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `OffsetGlobalIds` | Exodus wants global ids to start with 1, while VTK generally produces global ids starting with 0. Set this to true (default false), if the global ids are generated by VTK and hence start with 0. When writing to the output file, they will be offset by 1 to ensure the ids are valid exodus ids. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PreserveOriginalIds` | If input is transformed, e.g. through clipping, new element blocks may be created. This flag can be used to indicate whether to preserve the original ids from blocks or not. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `RemoveGhosts` | Property to control whether to remove ghost cells from the input or not. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `SideSetArrays` | Select the side set arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `SideSetSelectors` | Specify the side sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `WriteQAAndInformationRecords` | When checked, the writer will write quality assurance and information records, if available. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Output publication contract:

```json
{
  "comparison": "semantic",
  "extensions": [
    "exo"
  ],
  "filenames": "managed output directory",
  "losses": [
    "structure",
    "point-identity",
    "connectivity-order",
    "storage-type"
  ],
  "qualification": "requires fixture",
  "time": "one scheduled state"
}
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {
    "ChoosetheoutputblocksarraysfortheExodusEntityType": "no native command (GUI-only property)"
  },
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "explicit exports with semantic readback",
  "outputPorts": 0,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `scenes[].exports`; writers cannot be graph nodes. The main data input is `node`; non-data ports go in `resources`.

```json
{
  "id": "exportResult",
  "node": "DATA_NODE",
  "writer": "pvWriteIOSSWriter",
  "acceptLosses": [
    "structure",
    "point-identity",
    "connectivity-order",
    "storage-type"
  ]
}
```
